# WO-254: Every wizard sentence is in a string inventory
Status: queued (pre-approved: start when a WIP slot frees; note it on BOARD.md first)
Vendor: codex
Agent: app-tests (Felix Grant)
Kind: tests
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes (check-ins via CODEX_TO_CLAUDE.md)
Target release: next (never blocks a release)
Source: in-house coverage-gap batch 2026-11-09 (CLAUDE-064)
Worktree: `.vendor-wt/wo-254` on `vendor/wo-254` from main
Tracker: issue pending (in-house syncs freemyid-pm)

## Goal
The inventories are hand-kept, and nothing notices when in-house adds or moves wizard text. STRINGS.md's own header (line 3) warns that citations drift.

## Order
Start only after WO-225, WO-232 and WO-250 are merged (they write the inventories this test reads).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Using `ast` on the source text (no imports of wizard modules), collect string constants in `src/freemyid/wizard/*.py` that look like sentences a person sees: at least four words, start with a capital letter, end with `.`, `?` or `!`, or are values of `MSGS` (`src/freemyid/wizard/server.py:47`); skip docstrings and logger calls.
2. Each one appears (after normalising whitespace, curly/straight quotes and `{placeholders}`) in `docs/i18n/STRINGS.md`, `STRINGS_CLI.md` or `STRINGS_APP.md`, or in an EXCLUDED table in the test with a reason (for example mail-security copy kept out of scope by CLAUDE-024).
3. A KNOWN_GAPS list is allowed only with a reason per entry, and a second test fails when a KNOWN_GAPS entry no longer exists in the source, so the list can't go stale.
4. Every `src/...py:N` citation in those inventories points at a line range that contains at least one string literal.

Fake data only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Offline: no network, no sockets (FastAPI `TestClient` is fine), no git, no installs, no new dependencies. Tests must pass on Windows CI too: `tmp_path` and `pathlib`, no hard-coded `/tmp`, no `/`-joined path strings or other POSIX-only assumptions (WO-217 broke windows-latest that way). The module under test is outside Codex's code lane: a real product bug = `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` plus a finding with file:line in VENDOR_STATUS.md; never edit it. Check `tests/`, `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/` and `tests/grok/` first and don't duplicate a guard. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them in your worktree.
